key_insight: KAYRA packages an end-to-end, clinic-ready karyotyping pipeline as containerized microservices that combine semantic segmentation, instance detection and classification in a cascaded ROI-narrowing workflow to meet clinical operational constraints.
problem_solved: Automates chromosome-level karyotyping while addressing clinical-lab constraints (reproducible deployment, data privacy, limited local compute, and integration into existing workflows).
method: Containerized microservice pipeline that standardizes deployment (cloud and on‑premise) and orchestration of ML components.

Cascaded ROI‑narrowing strategy: semantic segmentation (EfficientNet‑B5 + U‑Net) → instance detection (Mask R‑CNN, ResNet‑50 + FPN) → classification (ResNet‑18) so each model focuses on progressively smaller, chromosome-bearing regions.
Same container images and service interfaces enable reproducible, modular upgrades and easier regulatory/operational adoption in clinical settings.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building clinical-grade ML systems that balance model accuracy with operational demands—useful for practitioners needing robust, deployable pipelines across cloud and on-premise environments.

paper_title: KAYRA: A Microservice Architecture for AI-Assisted Karyotyping with Cloud and On-Premise Deployment
paper_authors: Attila Pintér, Javier Rico, Attila Répai, Jalal Al-Afandi, Adrienn Éva Borsy
